clue.text: A lot of actors with provincial accents on the radio

parts.note: a broad accent is a strong regional one, so speech with provincial accents is broad
the cast of a play is its whole company of actors

explanation.surface: A troupe of players with regional voices performing over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transmitted by radio is sent out over the air to listeners.

clue.text: Oil platform supported by a Baltic port

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, held up from below

parts.note: a drilling rig is an offshore oil platform

explanation.surface: An offshore drilling platform propped up by a harbour city on the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latvian capital stands on the Gulf of Riga, a major Baltic harbour.

clue.text: Seized on pronouncement regarding succession of William fine

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the phrase is said out loud

parts.note: when King William III died, Queen Anne followed him on the throne, so she came next

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed power after declaring the royal line of succession settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'Anne next' runs together into a word for taken over by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory that is annexed is taken over and incorporated by force.

clue.text: Creditor, like a debtor, boasting of achievement

parts.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit or creditor
a debtor is someone owing money

explanation.surface: A lender gloating, as if he were the one in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowing is loud, triumphant bragging, like a cockerel's call.

clue.text: Land for one in the sun

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ground set aside for someone in a sunny spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is earth or ground, as in one's native land.

clue.text: Tradesman who got black looks when they brushed up

definitions.text: Tradesman who got black looks when they brushed up

parts.words: Tradesman who got black looks when they brushed up
parts.note: sounds like workers treated with disapproval, but these workers literally came out sooty-faced after pushing brushes up flues

explanation.surface: Workers who were frowned upon whenever they tidied themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: Flue cleaners pushed brushes up the stack and emerged covered in soot.

clue.text: Doubtless they lead to the heart of the countryside

definitions.text: Doubtless they lead to the heart of the countryside

parts.words: Doubtless they lead to the heart of the countryside
parts.note: plays on main routes as blood vessels leading to the heart, here a nation's heart

explanation.surface: A claim that certain routes surely take you deep into rural areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Major highways are named after arteries, the main vessels of the bloodstream.

clue.text: Their one old G&S production on stage

definitions.text: Their one old G&S production on stage

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of these letters, reassembling them

parts.note: G&S stands for Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera partnership

explanation.surface: A theatre company staging their one vintage Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta about Venetian boatmen while its first words are rearranged to spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: This operetta about two Venetian boatmen is one of the best-known Savoy operas by Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Welcome sign of approaching senility

parts.note: a gesture of greeting, read cryptically as a trembling hand that signals old age

explanation.surface: A doctor remarks that a certain symptom shows old age creeping up.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp of palms is a greeting, and a tremor in the palm hints at frailty.

clue.text: On the other hand, it is an admission that wisdom is not a monopoly

definitions.text: it is an admission that wisdom is not a monopoly

explanation.surface: Grudgingly conceding that one is not the only clever person around.
explanation.definitionFit: Means alternatively; split in two it says that others are clever too, conceding nobody owns good sense.

clue.text: It fights Mary quite contrary

indicators.note: from the nursery rhyme, contrary suggests the letters of the name being turned awkwardly about

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme girl described as a combative force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' is an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A military force made up of soldiers is what wages war on land.

clue.text: Lower wild flower?

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, a cow or bullock, so the flower is named after a mooing beast, like the cowslip

explanation.surface: Asking for a wildflower that grows nearer the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale yellow primula is a wild woodland plant closely related to the cowslip.

clue.text: Warm up before the final contest

explanation.surface: Athletes loosening up ahead of the deciding race.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm is to raise temperature; a qualifying round is run before a final.

clue.text: Scope for a doctor with sex appeal

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Room for manoeuvre for an attractive physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent, the bounds within which something operates.

clue.text: Celebrations presented by half of Galashiels

indicators.note: half of the town's ten-letter name means its opening five letters are kept

explanation.surface: Festivities put on by a Scottish Borders town.
explanation.walkthrough: Galashiels is a town in the Scottish Borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive occasions or grand parties are celebrations.

clue.text: Had a nightmare which put me in fear

indicators.note: put, with in, says one piece is placed into the other here
in completes the instruction to place the small word inside the word for fear

parts.note: dread is great fear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describing a bad night that left them terrified.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bad dream is to experience visions while asleep.

clue.text: Tearing in shreds a proverbially tough material

indicators.note: something torn in shreds is broken up, so the word's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Ripping into pieces something famously hard to break.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard igneous rock is a byword for toughness, as in 'granite-hard'.

clue.text: Derogatory title sought by writer whose pen lacks point

definitions.text: Derogatory title sought by writer whose pen lacks point

parts.words: Derogatory title sought by writer whose pen lacks point
parts.note: a mocking name for a self-important man, read as a writer hunting for missing metal pen tips

explanation.surface: A scornful nickname wanted by an author whose writing lacks sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular mock title for a self-important man, and literally a pen-writer's tips.

clue.text: Polish part of the missiles I aim

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Polish soldier describing the weapons he directs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a verb or adjective; it defines a region that is largely in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic region now lies mostly within Poland, so it is a Polish area.

clue.text: Fence in a pig to eat

indicators.note: the barrier word goes inside the word for the pig

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a wall is a barrier, like a fence

explanation.surface: Penning a hog so it can feed.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp food down the throat is to consume it.

clue.text: Leave the port when social cliques become ill

parts.note: sets are exclusive social circles
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Departing the harbour when fashionable circles fall sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships raise canvas and put to sea when departing harbour.

clue.text: Sort of pain caused by broken knee

indicators.note: a broken joint is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp ache from an injured knee.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen pain is sharp or acute, like a keen blade.

clue.text: The Church fabric

explanation.surface: Material bought for a parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are collectively 'the cloth', after clerical dress; it also means woven material.

clue.text: Tasks for men of patience

explanation.surface: Chores fit only for very tolerant people.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties to do; Job of the Bible was proverbially patient, so patient men are his namesakes.

clue.text: One time one-time

explanation.surface: A phrase repeated with only a hyphen added.
explanation.definitionFit: On a single occasion; also an adjective meaning former.

clue.text: A sign that women have lost their head

indicators.note: losing a head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: Ladies panicking is taken as a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or signal of things to come.

clue.text: A ship a sand-arm wrecked -many such ships in fact

indicators.note: a wrecked vessel is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vessel ran aground on a spit of sand, the fate of many in a famous fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1588 invasion fleet sent against England lost many ships wrecked on British coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1588 fleet sent against England lost many vessels wrecked on rocky coasts.

clue.text: Docking requires explanation of the fine points

explanation.surface: Mooring a boat needs careful instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off an animal's tail is docking; setting out particulars is explaining specifics.
